subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should experimental `claws add` be allowed to install or reuse process-wide ClawHub plugins under an exact displayed consent plan, or should plugin mutation wait for a separate host-level grant or isolation model?
rationale: The implementation deliberately chooses a shared-host resource model rather than agent isolation, and that choice changes the authority granted by creating a Claw; source review alone cannot select the intended product/security boundary.

options.title: Defer shared-plugin mutation
options.body: Keep workspace-scoped skills, but leave plugin package declarations fail-closed until maintainers approve a distinct host-level grant or isolation contract.

options.title: Approve the explicit shared-host model
options.body: Accept process-wide plugin installation only with the current exact-plan disclosure plus fresh live proof of install, reuse, conflict, and compensation behavior.

options.title: Require an isolation design
options.body: Pause this slice until plugins can be scoped per agent or otherwise constrained by a stronger runtime boundary.

recommendation.title: Defer shared-plugin mutation
recommendation.body: Keep workspace-scoped skills, but leave plugin package declarations fail-closed until maintainers approve a distinct host-level grant or isolation contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review directly frames the multi-agent consumer and shared-host safety tradeoff that needs an explicit direction decision.
